headline: Biological resources scale with structure-aware annotation, search, and AI-assisted access
label: Biological Database Infrastructure
summary: November 2026 updates to OMA, OrthoDB, VEuPathDB, BFVD and RNA structure resources add structure-based comparison and larger genome and structure coverage.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the expansion and re-engineering of public biological resources. OMA 2027 covers 2983 extant and 1226 ancestral genomes with structure-aware orthology (3Di, structural alignments). OrthoDB 2026 spans 5768 eukaryotic genomes, recomputes orthologous groups with MMseqs2 and a protein-LM alphabet (TEA), and rebuilds BUSCO lineages. VEuPathDB lists 2,602 datasets, AI-assisted curation and a PostgreSQL migration. Structural content is also growing: BFVD v3 offers predicted viral protein structures, RR3DD 2.0 classifies 15,764 RNA chains, and GTalign now handles nucleic acid 3D structure search and alignment. RNAhub2 uses prefiltering and NAF compression for scalable RNA homology search. ABAQS scores genome annotation quality. PhageScope 2.0, UHVDB and vartracker cover phage, virome and pathogen variant analysis. New elements are structure-informed comparison and AI-agent or AI-assisted access layers.
